subject: SLA and support terms — uptime & credits negotiation
messages:

Subject: Proposed SLA redlines - MSA & Order Form

Monica —

Attached are our initial redlines to the MSA/Order Form specifically for the SLA and support sections. High-level asks from Acme legal/procurement:

- Uptime target: 99.95% monthly for the Hosted API.
- Service credits: sliding scale, up to 20% of monthly fees depending on downtime.
- Response times: Sev1 initial response within 30 minutes, engaged engineering within 2 hours.
- Maintenance windows: exclude routine maintenance under 4 hours per week; require 72 hours notice for any planned maintenance affecting >5% of requests.
- Require rollback guarantees for major changes and audit logs for all incidents.

We understand some of these may be larger asks; please let us know Redwood's position and any alternate language you prefer. We included a marked-up doc: Acme_SLA_redlines_v1.docx.

Can we schedule a legal sync next week to narrow these down? Tom

Subject: Re: Proposed SLA redlines - MSA & Order Form

Tom — thanks for sending these over. I pulled the key asks and looped in engineering and our commercial/ops leads. Quick response in advance of a sync:

- Uptime: Redwood is generally comfortable with a 99.9% uptime commitment for hosted customers on the Order Form. 99.95% is technically possible but materially changes pricing and capacity reservations; we can provide a costed option if Acme wants that.
- Credits: we prefer a capped credit model (10% cap monthly) rather than an uncapped sliding scale; we'll propose specific tiers in the counter.
- Response times: 30-minute acknowledge for Sev1 is aggressive for a distributed SaaS + dedicated infra contract; we propose initial ack within 60 minutes and an active engineering engagement within 2 hours.
- Maintenance windows: we typically schedule planned maintenance with 7 days notice and a typical window of 2 hours, up to 4 hours for major upgrades. We do not guarantee zero-impact for emergency security patches.
- Rollback: we can commit to rollback when possible, with documented rollback procedures and incident audit logs.

I attached our inline comments: Redwood_SLA_comments_v1.docx.

Can we take a 30-minute legal + ops call Tue 17 Mar? If that works I will send a calendar invite and a clean counter-offer beforehand.

Thanks,
Monica
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: feasibility notes on Acme SLA asks

Monica / Priyom — a few engineering notes to feed the counter:

- 99.95% vs 99.9%: moving from 99.9% to 99.95% reduces allowable monthly downtime from ~43.2 minutes to ~21.6 minutes. To reliably meet 99.95 we need dedicated extra capacity and changes to maintenance cadence; that will increase cost ~15-25% depending on region.
- Credits: uncapped credits are risky; recommend a capped sliding scale (e.g., 5% for <99.7, 10% for 99.0-99.7, 15% for <99.0) and an annual cap so a single incident doesn't wipe out revenue.
- Response SLAs: 60-min initial response for Sev1 is doable with on-call rotations but we should avoid a hard engineering-resolve time guarantee — we can commit to response/engagement times and time-to-mitigation targets where possible.
- Maintenance windows: ops team typically schedules monthly maintenance blocks ~2 hours; we can support up to 4 hours for major upgrades but not weekly 4-hour windows. Recommend language: scheduled maintenance (up to 4 hours/month) with 7 days notice; emergency maintenance with best-effort notice and no credits unless caused by Redwood negligence.
- Fallback/rollback: we can offer an automatic fallback to a compatible model variant or region-level routing during incidents, but that should be treated as an operational mitigation rather than a contractual uptime guarantee.

If you want, I can draft a short technical appendix describing our incident mitigation and rollback timelines for the counter.

Rishi
VP, Platform Engineering (on-call)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tom Erickson <tom.erickson@acme.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@acme.com>, Procurement <procurement@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 11:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood counterproposal: SLA & support language (MSA/Order Form)

Tom / Acme team — thanks for the initial redlines and for the patience while we validated operational feasibility. Attached is Redwood's formal counter (Redwood_SLA_Counter_v2.docx). Key points summarized below so the legal call is focused:

Proposed SLA and support summary (Redwood counter)
- Uptime target: 99.9% monthly for Hosted API (Order Form).
- Service credits: tiered/capped model; maximum credit 10% of monthly fees for a single billing period. Credits applied as a percentage of that month’s fees only; annual cumulative cap of 20% (we are open to discussing a different annual cap).
- Incident response:
  - Severity 1 (system unavailable for customer production traffic): initial acknowledgement within 60 minutes; engineering engaged and mitigation plan within 2 hours.
  - Severity 2 (degraded functionality impacting many users): initial acknowledgement within 4 hours; workaround plan within 24 hours.
  - Severity 3 (minor impact): acknowledgement within 24 hours.
- Maintenance: scheduled maintenance with 7 days notice; typical window 2 hours, up to 4 hours for major upgrades (cumulative up to 4 hours/month). Emergency maintenance for security patches with best-effort notice; emergency maintenance does not automatically trigger credits unless caused by Redwood negligence.
- Rollback & mitigation: Redwood will document rollback procedures and provide incident logs and a post-incident report for Sev1 incidents. Automated regional fallback and model-variant routing are available as operational mitigations.

We propose a 30-minute legal + ops sync on Tue, 17 Mar at 10:00 AM PT to walk through the attached redline and align on the remaining open items (credits annual cap, rollback language, and emergency maintenance carveouts). I've included HubSpot and DocuSign prefill links in the related links for convenience.

Attachments: Redwood_SLA_Counter_v2.docx

Thanks — look forward to resolving the outstanding points on the call.

Best,
Monica Patel
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
